newsitem.title: INDIA: India spot rupee ends down vs dlr, forwards ease.
newsitem.headline: India spot rupee ends down vs dlr, forwards ease.

text.p: The Indian rupee dropped sharply in late afternoon trade on Monday on sustained dollar buying by a leading state-run bank based in eastern India, dealers said.
The rupee ended Monday at 35.89/90 per dollar after trading in a narrow 35.79/81 range for most of the day, they said.
The rupee had opened the day at 35.79/80 per dollar.
"It (the state-run bank) was in the market in a big way in late afternoon," said a dealer.

"There was no other reason for the rupee's fall today." Dealers, while uncertain about the reasons for the bank's dollar purchases on Monday, said it could have been on account of payments by state-run fimrs, particularly oil firms.

"Most of these companies are its (the bank's) clients," a dealer said. "With the year-end coming up, there must be a fair amount of payments to be made and this could be the reason for today's purchases."
A dealer at a foreign bank said he felt the rupee would regain on a technical correction on Tuesday.
"We saw some dollar selling in the late evening," he said. "I think some banks may be long and there could be a correction tomorrow."
Dealers said the Reserve Bank of India was not active in the spot market and its intervention on Monday was by way of swaps.
"It was rolling over swaps maturing in December," said a dealer. "This pushed premia down a bit."
"Overall the sentiment remains soft," he said. "With RBI receiving premia, we can expect premia to remain easy."
The premium for six-month forward dollars ended Monday at an annualised 7.47 percent against the weekend close of 7.55 percent, dealers said.
